_comment: Narration voices for `manim-kit render --voice` and `manim-kit voice say`.
Text only: the Phonon models and voice embeddings are fetched into the Hugging Face
cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub) on first use or by `manim-kit voice setup`, pinned
to the Hub revisions in the phonon section below, never committed.
A spec string is 'backend:voice' or 'backend:voice:lang'. The default below is
fleet-wide, because this repo is synced to every host. $MANIM_KIT_VOICE overrides
it per host or per shell, and `--voice SPEC` overrides both.
Two backends (user decision 2026-10-26, replacing kokoro-v1): phonon runs gradium's
Phonon 40M multilingual offline on the CPU, English and German, and is the default.
Its output is CC BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial only, credit 'Phonon by Gradium, CC BY-NC 4.0'.
When 40M cannot load, English falls back to Phonon 31M English (Apache-2.0, same voice
names); German then fails. Commercial work uses gemini-flash-tts, which calls the API
and costs money. Piper, gTTS and edge-tts stay out - see NARRATION-DESIGN.md.
Old kokoro-v1:<id> specs still work: phonon.kokoro maps each Kokoro voice to the
Phonon voice of the same accent and gender (af_heart -> Hadley, af_sarah -> Harper).
Gemini billing: $1 per 1M input text tokens plus $20 per 1M audio output tokens,
about $0.006 for a two-sentence narration line.
language_defaults maps a bare language code to a spec, so `--voice de` or
MANIM_KIT_VOICE=de picks the German default. User decision 2026-10-26:
Harper for English, Annika for German, both Phonon.

phonon.label: Phonon 40M multilingual (ptts), fallback Phonon 31M English
phonon.licence: 40M: CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial only, credit 'Phonon by Gradium, CC BY-NC 4.0'. 31M English: Apache-2.0. ptts runtime: MIT or Apache-2.0.
phonon.note: Offline, 24 kHz, English and German. The 40M model is gated on Hugging Face: the first download needs a token whose account accepted its terms.

gemini-flash-tts.label: Gemini TTS
gemini-flash-tts.note: 24 kHz PCM. Needs GEMINI_API_KEY. A leading instruction sentence is read as a directive, not spoken.

voices.note: Default. American female, adult, confident and friendly.

German default. German female, adult, sparky and attentive.

Lively male voice. Best prosody of the English options, and it costs money.
Calm female voice, good for a long explainer.
German female voice, firm and clear. The German choice for commercial work, paid.
German female voice, softer than Kore.
